papers.title_in_file: An unconditional distribution learning advantage with shallow quantum circuits
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, sections II to V (preliminaries, sampling-to-learning, summary and discussion); appendix proofs only skimmed by theorem statements.
papers.what_it_is: A theory paper proving a PAC generator-learning separation between constant-depth quantum circuits and constant-depth bounded fan-in classical circuits.

assertions.value: The paper proves an unconditional quantum advantage in PAC distribution learning: constant-depth quantum circuits with one and two qubit gates (QNC0) are superior to constant-depth bounded fan-in classical circuits (NC0) as hypothesis classes.
quotes: we prove an unconditional quantum advantage in the probably approximately correct (PAC) distribution learning framework with shallow quantum circuit hypotheses
constant-depth quantum circuits using one and two qubit gates (QNC0) are superior compared to constant-depth bounded fan-in classical circuits (NC0) as a choice for hypothesis classes
assertions.certainty_reason: Main theorem, summarized in the abstract and Theorem III.1 with Theorem 7, pp.1-6

assertions.value: The paper proves (Theorem III.1) a polynomial-time PAC generator learning algorithm that outputs a constant-depth quantum circuit, and states the quantum circuit can be learned from examples to perfect precision.
quotes: outputs a description of a constant-depth quantum circuit whose Born distribution
we can learn that circuit from examples to perfect precision
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem III.1 (restated as Theorem 12 in the appendix)

assertions.value: The authors state the problem uses highly structured data, that advantages over deeper classical circuits remain to be shown, and that the result is a stepping stone.
quotes: Ideally, one should be able to show advantages also over deeper classical circuits.
it still makes use of highly structured data
this result is a stepping stone in a bigger program
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' own statement of limits in Section V
assertions.reader_inference: The separation is against constant-depth classical circuits only; it does not speak to deep classical models or to practical unstructured data.

papers.title_in_file: The QuaST Decision Tree: Achieving Automation With Data-Based Recommendations
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, feasibility analysis summary, usage scenarios, Section VIII (MaxCut demonstration), Section IX discussion; framework design sections skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A software-framework paper presenting a modular decision-tree for hybrid quantum-classical optimization with a module that judges variational algorithm feasibility.

assertions.value: In a MaxCut demonstration with n = 60 variables, the authors report that only VQE with the optimizers NGD and Powell produce feasible options, and that the module recommends VQE with NGD.
quotes: As a demonstration, a MaxCut instance with n = 60 variables
Of all configurations evaluated, only VQE with the optimizers NGD and Powell produce feasible options.
the module recommends VQE with NGD as the optimal configuration
assertions.certainty_reason: One demonstration instance in a single framework paper; empirical

assertions.value: The authors report that all QAOA-based variants either exhibit extreme shot requirements or cannot be characterized, and that most fail to produce characterizable scaling behavior.
quotes: All QAOAbased variants, including vanilla QAOA, ma-QAOA, QAOA+, DC-QAOA, and WS-QAOA, either exhibit extreme shot requirements or cannot be characterized.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single demonstration instance; empirical

assertions.value: The authors define feasibility by a quantum disadvantage boundary: a configuration whose shot requirements exceed this boundary is outperformed by exhaustive classical search.
quotes: a hard feasibility criterion comes from the quantum disadvantage boundary
Any configuration where shot requirements exceed this boundary is outperformed by exhaustive classical search.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own definition of the criterion

assertions.value: The authors state that validation is initial: two scenarios are validated, commercial solver integration is left as future work, and the crucial next step is validation at increasing technology readiness.
quotes: Initial validation is provided for two scenarios, with the commercial solver integration left as future work.
The crucial next development step in the QDT is its validation at increasing technology readiness, moving towards productive environments.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' own statement of scope and status

papers.title_in_file: Photonic Time-Delayed Quantum Extreme Learning Machine
papers.what_it_is: A short letter proposing and numerically simulating a silicon-photonic quantum extreme learning machine, tested on the two moons benchmark.

assertions.value: In simulation on the two moons task, the authors report a test accuracy of 0.85 for a linear classifier on the encoded phases and 0.96 when the quantum substrate is used as a preprocessing layer.
quotes: the linear classifier achieves a test accuracy of 0.85 and produces a linear decision boundary
Using the quantum substrate as a preprocessing layer increases the test accuracy to 0.96
assertions.certainty_reason: Single simulated benchmark

assertions.value: The authors report that the full Fock distribution gives a mean accuracy of 0.9682, slightly below the estimated Bayes-optimal accuracy of 0.971.
quotes: Using the complete Fock distribution, the model achieves an accuracy of 0.9682
The mean accuracy remains slightly below the estimated Bayes-optimal accuracy of 0.971
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation on one toy benchmark

assertions.value: The authors report that eleven features reach near-optimal performance with an accuracy of 0.9665, and that under simulated losses of 1 and 2 dB the model keeps comparable accuracy.
quotes: reaches near-optimal performance with eleven features, yielding an accuracy of 0.9665
The BS gate transmissivity is chosen to reproduce total losses of 1 and 2 dB.
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulated; loss modeled by beam splitter

assertions.value: The paper evaluates the architecture by numerical simulation with the Strawberry Fields Gaussian backend, on the two-moons benchmark as a proof of concept.
quotes: We theoretically demonstrate the reservoir's computational capability through binary classification of the non-linear two moons benchmark.
Numerical simulations were performed using the Strawberry Fields Gaussian backend
As a proof of concept, we consider the standard two-moons classification benchmark
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' statement of their own setup

papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, section 2 model descriptions, sections 3.4-3.5 (noise model, results), start of section 4 theory, section 5 conclusion; proofs in section 4 skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A simulation study of a variational quantum classifier with Hamming-distance measurement and post-processing that filters ambiguous outcomes.

assertions.value: The authors report, on a breast cancer dataset in a 3-qubit noiseless setting, an average accuracy of 90% for the unambiguous classifier, 6.9 percentage points above the best baseline, with eight times fewer circuit executions per prediction.
quotes: The unambiguous classifier achieves an average accuracy of 90%, corresponding to an improvement of 6.9 percentage points over the baseline, while requiring eight times fewer circuit executions per prediction.
in a 3-qubit noiseless setting, the proposed classifier achieves an average accuracy of 90%, outperforming the best-performing baseline by 6.9 percentage points
assertions.certainty_reason: One dataset, simulation

assertions.value: The authors report that under simulated noise the improvement falls to approximately 3.1 percentage points and the 3-qubit accuracy of the best model drops to 65.72%.
quotes: In the presence of noise, the improvement is reduced to approximately 3.1 percentage points, with the same reduction in execution cost.
In the noisy setting, the accuracy of the bestperforming model, M3, drops to 65.72%
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulated noise channels with large error probabilities

assertions.value: The authors report that the unambiguous classifier performs worse on 5 qubits than on 3 qubits, with an average accuracy of 76.84% noiseless and 62.31% under noise.
quotes: model M3 performs worse on 5 qubits than on 3 qubits
with an average accuracy of 76.84% in the noiseless setup and 62.31% under noisy conditions
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation, one dataset

assertions.value: The authors state that the study covers one breast cancer dataset and that future work will extend the approach to larger systems and more complex datasets.
quotes: We evaluate the proposed method on a breast cancer classification dataset.
Future work will focus on extending the approach to larger systems and more complex datasets
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' own statement of scope

papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, section on Q-RUN formulation and Claim 2, relaxed implementation, selected experiment results, conclusion; appendices and most tables skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A classical neural-network layer inspired by data re-uploading quantum circuits, evaluated on classical data-modeling and prediction tasks.

assertions.value: The authors report that Q-RUN reduces model parameters while decreasing error by approximately one to three orders of magnitude on certain tasks, compared with fully connected layers and other network layers.
quotes: Q-RUN reduces model parameters while decreasing error by approximately one to three orders of magnitude on certain tasks
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical results of one study

assertions.value: The paper states (as a claim with a proof sketch) that under optimal conditions Q-RUN can express a d-dimensional truncated Fourier series with up to 3dn frequency components.
quotes: Under optimal conditions, Q-RUN is capable of expressing a d-dimensional truncated Fourier series with a frequency spectrum containing up to 3dn components.
assertions.certainty_reason: Only a sketch of proof is given; conditions are stated as optimal

assertions.value: The authors state that Q-RUN replaces quantum measurement with a lightweight MLP approximation and that their goal is not to outperform task-specific, highly specialized models.
quotes: we relax the strict reliance on quantum measurements in their theoretical form and instead introduce a lightweight MLP to approximate the measurement process
our goal is not to outperform task-specific, highly specialized models
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' statement of their own scope

assertions.value: The authors report that on the fourth dataset of a model-size study Q-RUN shows a U-shaped trend, with error first decreasing then increasing, indicating potential overfitting at larger capacities.
quotes: On the fourth dataset, however, Q-RUN exhibits a less ideal U-shaped trend. The MSE first decreases and then increases, indicating potential overfitting at larger capacities.
assertions.certainty_reason: One experiment

papers.title_in_file: Benchmarking loss functions for trainable quantum feature maps
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, sections II-III, start of section IV, section V noise subsection, conclusion; dataset tables skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A simulation benchmark of three loss functions for training trainable quantum feature maps in quantum SVMs.

assertions.value: The authors report that the Log-Likelihood Loss consistently achieves more stable optimization than Measurement Loss while retaining linear computational complexity.
quotes: Our results show that Log-Likelihood Loss consistently achieves more stable optimization than Measurement Loss while retaining linear computational complexity.
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical experiments on benchmark datasets

assertions.value: The authors state that Distance Loss needs fidelity evaluations for all pairs of training samples, so its cost grows quadratically with data size, and that Measurement Loss is linear but suffers a trajectory crossing problem.
quotes: the DL method requires fidelity evaluations for all pairs of training samples
the ML method achieves linear scaling
a recurring optimization phenomenon that we refer to as trajectory crossing problem
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' analysis and observation in their experiments

assertions.value: Under simulated noise, the authors report that accuracy on the moons dataset is almost unchanged, while it decreases by approximately 0.06 and 0.09 for the circles and gaussian datasets.
quotes: The performance on the moons dataset remains almost unchanged, while the accuracy decreases by approximately 0.06 and 0.09 for the circles and gaussian datasets, respectively.
All previous results were obtained using an ideal noisefree statevector simulator.
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulated noise model, fixed layer count

assertions.value: The authors state that the framework still relies on a classical SVM for the final decision boundary and that it remains unclear whether improvements come from the number of trainable parameters or the ansatz structure.
quotes: the current framework still relies on a classical SVM classifier for the final decision boundary
it remains unclear whether the observed improvements are mainly determined by the number of trainable parameters or by the structural properties of the quantum ansatz
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' own statement in the conclusion

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Generative Adversarial Autoencoders: Learning latent representations for quantum data generation
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results for H2 and LiH, conclusion and open questions; methods and appendices skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A simulation paper proposing a quantum model that learns the latent space of a quantum autoencoder with a quantum GAN, tested on entangled states and molecular ground states.

assertions.value: The authors report average energy errors of 0.02 Ha for H2 and 0.06 Ha for LiH from the trained QGAA, in simulations up to 6 qubits.
quotes: The average errors in the energies estimated by the trained QGAA are 0.02 Ha for H2 and 0.06 Ha for LiH in simulations upto 6 qubits.
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation, small systems

assertions.value: The authors report that the LiH results are comparatively suboptimal, which they attribute primarily to limitations in the trained encoder.
quotes: In contrast, the results for LiH are comparatively suboptimal, primarily due to limitations in the trained encoder, as reported in Table I.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' attribution, not tested separately

assertions.value: The authors state that the implementations were limited to small-scale quantum systems, the largest being 6 qubits for LiH, and that experiments were run on simulators.
quotes: The implementations explored in this study were limited to small-scale quantum systems with the largest being 6 qubits for the LiH molecule.
While our experiments were conducted on simulators
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' own statement of scope

assertions.value: The authors state that although quantum adversarial learning theory guarantees a unique Nash equilibrium, they met practical challenges in steering the model toward it during training.
quotes: Although the theory of quantum adversarial learning guarantees the existence of a unique Nash equilibrium, we encountered practical challenges in steering the model toward this optimal solution during training.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' own report of a training limitation

papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results (data size, QPU comparison, RFF/ELM comparison), discussion; supplementary material skimmed by search.
papers.what_it_is: A study using boson-sampling output distributions as a reservoir feature map for classical classifiers, with simulations and runs on a Quandela photonic processor.

assertions.value: In simulation with a perfect single photon source, the authors report that QORC surpasses the best test accuracy of multinomial logistic regression at around 2,500 training images, against the 60,000 images the regression needs for peak performance.
quotes: QORC surpasses the maximally possible testing accuracy of MLR (black dashed) at around 2,500 training images for a perfect noiseless single photon source
compared to the 60,000 images used to reach peak performance in the MLR
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical, one study, MNIST

assertions.value: The authors report collecting distribution samples for 4,669 MNIST images from a physical Quandela Ascella QPU and state that its performance is close to ideal, with a small residual attributed to device imperfections.
quotes: Finally, we collected distribution samples for 4,669 MNIST images from a physical QPU
This close to ideal performance of the physical QPU is also supported by Fig. 2(b)
leaving a small but statistically significant residual, which we attribute to device imperfections not captured by our noise model
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical, one device
assertions.reader_inference: The QPU supplies the reservoir sampling; the classifier is still trained classically.

assertions.value: The authors report that Random Fourier Features reach a similar improvement to QORC, while an extreme learning machine yields a more modest gain below QORC.
quotes: As shown in Table I, RFF reaches a similar improvement to QORC, while ELM yields a more modest gain, clearly below our scheme.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical comparison on MNIST
assertions.reader_inference: A classical fixed random feature map matches the gain, so the gain may not be specific to quantum resources.

assertions.value: The authors state that the work is on static toy-model image data and that advancing both hardware implementation and task diversity will be key to realising concrete quantum advantage in real-world machine learning tasks.
quotes: Extending our framework beyond static toy model image data
Ultimately, advancing both the hardware implementation and task diversity of QORC will be key to realising concrete quantum advantage in real-world machine learning tasks.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' own statement of scope and future work
